forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: City of London Police forecasts £1.66m underspend on £126.0m budget, helped by £6.8m in pay savings
news_drafts.lead:
City of London Police is forecasting that it will spend £1.66m less than its budget this year, according to first-quarter budget monitoring (the in-year check of spending against budget) reported to the City of London Police Authority Board on 14 October. The underspend is 1.3% of a £126.0m budget.

The papers attribute most of it to £6.8m of savings on workforce pay. Recruitment delays and lower staffing than budgeted meant the money set aside for officers and staff exceeded actual costs, even with what the paper calls significant recruitment activity. Officer and staff numbers remain below budgeted levels. The pay underspends have been used to cover cost pressures arising during the year.

The papers say the position "remains dependent upon temporary vacancy-related savings which are expected to reduce as recruitment progresses". They add that the savings "are not expected to be sustainable in the longer term". The force says it needs to review its cost pressures through the 2027/28 budget-setting process.

findings.committee: City of London Police Authority Board
findings.paper_title: Revenue & Capital Budget Monitoring - Slide Deck (1)
findings.headline: Slower than anticipated external recruitment, with approximately 50% internal appointments, keeping workforce below budgeted levels
findings.detail: Staff workforce forecast assumes lower staffing than budgeted due to slower external recruitment linked partly to approximately 50% of appointments being internal moves. Internal appointments do not increase overall organisation strength. This recruitment challenge contributes to both current vacancy-driven savings and future sustainability risks.
findings.matters: Identifies constraint on ability to build staffing levels; directly related to sustainability of current vacancy savings and underlying operational capacity issues.
findings.figures: Approximately 50% internal appointments; staff workforce forecast lower than budgeted
findings.quote: The staff workforce forecast assumes that both the core and temporary funded strength will be lower than budgeted due to slower than anticipated external recruitment linked, in part, to c50% internal appointments

findings.committee: City of London Police Authority Board
findings.paper_title: Revenue & Capital Budget Monitoring - Slide Deck (1)
findings.headline: Emerging capital investment pressures identified for ERP replacement, Fleet Strategy and Future Police Estate IT, financial impact to be reported in subsequent periods
findings.detail: Beyond current 26/27 capital programme (£5.4m budget, £5.1m forecast), additional significant investment pressures have been identified but not yet quantified. These include ERP system replacement, Fleet Strategy investment recommendations and Future Police Estate IT network rollout. Future Police Estate Programme requires £3.3m technology investment commitment, with £1.1m transferred to reserves in 26/27.
findings.matters: Emerging capital affordability risk for future years; unquantified pressures suggest potential impact on medium-term financial planning and borrowing requirements.
findings.figures: Future Police Estate: £3.3m total technology investment commitment (£1.1m transferred to reserves in 26/27); whole life programme £69.9m budget vs £69.5m forecast
findings.quote: Several additional cost risk pressures have been identified and are currently being assessed, with the financial impact expected to be reported in subsequent periods once qualified

findings.committee: City of London Police Authority Board
findings.paper_title: Revenue & Capital Budget Monitoring - Slide Deck (1)
findings.headline: Local Government Pension Scheme employer contribution rate reduced from 21% to 20%, delivering £380k annual saving
findings.detail: Rate reduction from 1 April 2026 reflects higher-than-expected pension fund investment returns. Results in estimated £380k per annum saving with no impact on staff pay or accrued benefits, supporting organisational affordability.
findings.matters: Positive development reducing ongoing cost base and improving medium-term financial sustainability.
findings.figures: Rate reduced from 21% to 20%; £380k pa saving
findings.quote: Local Government Pension Scheme (LGPS) employer contribution: rate reduced from 21% to 20% from 1 April 2026. This is estimated to result in a saving of £380k pa

findings.committee: City of London Police Authority Board
findings.paper_title: Revenue & Capital Budget Monitoring - Slide Deck (1)
findings.headline: Staff pay settlement of 3.5% under negotiation with trade unions, against 3% planning assumption
findings.detail: Police officers received confirmed 3.5% pay award from 1 September 2026 (additional cost approximately £0.15m in-year, offset by Home Office grant). Staff are being offered 3.5% increase including consolidated London Weighting (planning assumption 3%), but negotiations with recognised trade unions remain ongoing.
findings.matters: Final settlement could exceed planned costs, affecting budget outturn and future year planning; staff costs less certain than officer costs which are grant-funded.
findings.figures: Officer pay: 3.5% vs 3% planning assumption; approximately £0.15m additional in-year (£0.26m full year), offset by Home Office grant
findings.quote: an offer has been made to include a 3.5% increase to base pay and London Weighting, subject to London Weighting being consolidated into base pay (planning assumption was 3%). Negotiations are continuing with recognised trade unions

findings.committee: City of London Police Authority Board
findings.paper_title: Revenue & Capital Budget Monitoring - Slide Deck (1)
findings.headline: £2.695m Home Office grant funding for Neighbourhood Policing conditional on achieving 62 FTE by 31 March 2027
findings.detail: Council must increase neighbourhood policing teams by 14 FTEs during 2026/27 to reach 62 total FTE by year-end, with achievement of this target being a condition of £2.695m grant funding. This creates a specific deadline and funding risk in context of noted recruitment lead times.
findings.matters: Conditional grant creates budget risk if target not achieved; given identified recruitment challenges, this is a material deadline-driven dependency.
findings.figures: 62 FTE target by 31 March 2027; £2.695m conditional grant funding; 14 FTE increase required in 26/27
findings.quote: £2.695m of Home Office grant funding is dependent on achieving a FTE of 62 NPT officers by 31 March 2027

daily_post.headline: IT access management deficiencies: one user has diagnostic tool access, three can both develop and implement changes
daily_post.lead: Weak segregation of duties in the financial system increases the risk of unauthorized changes to the general ledger or supporting controls. This is a material control environment issue.
